correctness.rationale: Prüfer occupancy proves exact conditional PMF including boundary cases. Uniform exchangeability forces the constant first moment. The Touchard-polynomial real-rootedness induction proves strict Stirling row log-concavity, giving the strict ratio monotonicity. Adjacent positive-cell likelihood ratios yield a unique sign transition; fixed means give all stop-loss inequalities, strict on the nontrivial range. First two Prüfer positions give the factorial moment and variance. Standalone exact arithmetic reproduced 448491 finite assertions, which is supplementary rather than a universal proof.

Wagner (2012 and 2014) proves central limit statements for random-tree additive functionals, and thus neither entails this exact conditional finite-size order.

The published-finding corpus Cayley-tree finding conditions degree on distance between marked vertices, a different global statistic. The recursive-tree finding has a different tree law and positive covariance of root degree with leaf count.

A generic total-positivity theorem could potentially dominate it, hence residual risk.

originality.rationale: Originality is limited to the all-strata one-marked-degree strict convex order, unique tail crossing, and their dependence consequences. Exact occupancy and tree-degree enumerations, Stirling real-rootedness, and mean symmetry are acknowledged as classical. The closest full primary arXiv text (Remmel–Williamson 2010) gives the exact fixed-leaf encoding but no convex/tail comparison; Wagner studies CLTs; current published-finding corpus near matches condition on different statistics or tree models. The ordering requires the separately proved strict Stirling ratio lemma and stop-loss argument. Unknown historical occupancy total positivity remains a candid priority risk.
residual_risks: Classical occupancy total-positivity literature may contain an equivalent conditional tagged-cell convex ordering under an alternative vocabulary.
Aldous (1990) and Wagner (2014) full publisher texts were not accessible, so abstract-level comparisons cannot eliminate hidden results.
Remmel–Williamson exact degree/leaf counts entail the conditional probability formula; novelty is in the quantified comparison, not the cell counts.

value.rationale: Leaf count is a canonical global invariant for random trees; tagged degree is a canonical local statistic. Zero conditional mean regression conceals strictly increasing convex degree dispersion and one sharp tail crossover as leaves increase, for every n and every admissible pair of leaf strata. This provides a structural all-threshold dependence law rather than an arbitrary finite tabulation or a routine extension of a single mean.
